summary: The rewrite passes spawn a `printf | grep -Fxq` pipeline for every line of the ledger, including headings, blanks and [fixed] entries, whenever anything is being annotated.
failure_scenario: A ledger with 1,500 lines and one auto-annotated entry costs about 3,000 process creations in pass 3 (printf in a pipeline subshell, plus the grep exec). `fi_annotate_apply_picks` pass B at line 154 does the same. Pass 2 repeats it per candidate, per touched file, per other candidate (lines 482 and 488). This runs from the post-commit hook on Windows Git Bash. Matching by text equality also means two identical lines are indistinguishable.
evidence: lib/annotate.sh:533 `if [[ -n "$auto_set" ]] && printf '%s' "$auto_set" | grep -Fxq -- "$line"; then`; lib/annotate.sh:154 same pattern; lib/annotate.sh:482 `printf '%s' "${cand_tfs[$j]}" | grep -Fxq -- "$tf"`
suggested_fix: Test membership with a builtin: keep `nl=$'\n'` and use `[[ "$nl$auto_set" == *"$nl$line$nl"* ]]` (auto_set already ends in newline). Better, record the ledger line numbers in pass 1 and compare numbers.

summary: Each candidate entry is parsed twice and then re-read with four more `printf|grep|head|cut` chains. `--pick` has no prefilter at all, so every [open] entry pays about 45 process creations.
failure_scenario: In `fi_annotate_auto`, a candidate runs `fi_parse_entry` (about 30 processes: sed, plus grep, sed and paste for each of six annotation kinds). It then runs four `printf|grep|head|cut` chains (about 16 processes). Then `fi_entry_loc` at line 448 runs `fi_parse_entry` again (about 45 more). That is roughly 90 processes per candidate on every `git commit`. In `fi_annotate_apply_picks` pass A (line 111), `fi_entry_loc` runs for ALL [open] entries before any selector is compared. A 100-entry ledger costs about 4,500 process creations for one `--pick`.
evidence: lib/annotate.sh:414 `e_data="$(fi_parse_entry "$line")"`, :415/:439/:440/:441 `printf '%s' "$e_data" | grep '^...=' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-`, :448 `loc="$(fi_entry_loc "$line")"` (re-parses); lib/annotate.sh:111 `loc="$(fi_entry_loc "$line")" || continue` with no prefilter
suggested_fix: Parse once and split the key=value output with a `while read` loop, as `fi_entry_to_json` does. Build the loc from the already-parsed fields. In pass A, skip lines that do not contain the selector's location text; `loc` is always a textual substring of the line.
needs_runtime_repro: Count process creations with a 100-entry ledger, e.g. `strace -f -c -e trace=execve found-issues annotate-commit HEAD --pick x:1`.

summary: Rename-plus-edit commits never match entries. Candidate matching uses the new path from `--name-only`, while `fi_diff_old_ranges` keys ranges by the old `---` path.
failure_scenario: Entry `- [open] ... lib/old.sh:40 — bug`. A commit renames lib/old.sh to lib/new.sh and edits line 40. `git show --name-only` and `gh pr view --json files` report only `lib/new.sh`. `tf == e_path` fails at line 427, so the entry is not a candidate and the output is 'no [open] entries match files touched'. The needed annotation is skipped silently. The reverse case also fails: after sync has rewritten the entry to the new path, the ranges are still keyed `lib/old.sh`, so `fi_line_matched` fails and hook mode reports 'cited line not touched'.
evidence: lib/annotate.sh:243-245 `p = substr($0, 5) ... cur = ...` (takes the `---` old path only; the `rename from/to` and `+++` lines are ignored); lib/annotate.sh:427 `if [[ "$tf" == "$e_path" || "$tf" == */"$e_path" || "$e_path" == */"$tf" ]]`
suggested_fix: Parse `rename from` / `rename to` (or the `+++` path) in the awk and emit both names. Also add the old name to touched_files via `git show --name-status -M`, or compare entries against either side.
needs_runtime_repro: Create a repo, log an entry on lib/old.sh:40, then `git mv lib/old.sh lib/new.sh`, edit line 40, commit, and run `found-issues annotate-commit HEAD --hook-auto`. Expected: a suggestion. Observed (predicted): 'no [open] entries match'.

summary: In hook mode, candidates whose cited line the commit did NOT touch are still listed, and the hook injects them as a 'needs annotation judgment' context. The mass-touch guard lists every candidate with no cap.
failure_scenario: A commit edits a hot file cited by 40 [open] entries, none of which have cited lines in the hunks. Each one becomes an `ambig_indices` item with reason 'cited line not touched by this change'. The command returns 3, and post-bash-dispatch.sh injects a 40-line block plus 'If this commit addresses any candidate, run...' into the agent context on EVERY such commit. Lines 520-523 do the same for all candidates when the mass-touch guard fires. The agent is told to judge entries the diff provably did not touch.
evidence: lib/annotate.sh:494-497 `ambig_reasons+=("cited line not touched by this change")`; :520-523 loop adds every candidate; :560-573 prints them all; hooks/post-bash-dispatch.sh:293-299 `elif [[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]]; then ctx+=...`
suggested_fix: In hook mode, drop 'cited line not touched' and 'scope-limited' items from the printed list and the return code (or cap the list at about 5 with a '+N more' line). Return 3 only when a genuinely line-matched but contested or mass-touched candidate exists.

summary: A failed or oversized `gh pr diff` is swallowed with `|| true`. Hook mode then reports every candidate as 'cited line not touched by this change' instead of saying the diff was unavailable.
failure_scenario: `gh pr diff N` fails on a transient error, rate limit or HTTP 406 'diff too large' (more than 20k lines). `old_ranges` is empty and `fi_line_matched` returns 1 for everything. Every PR-auto suggestion is silently lost, and the agent is shown misleading per-entry reasons.
evidence: lib/annotate-commands.sh:151 `old_ranges="$(gh pr diff "$pr_num" 2>/dev/null | fi_diff_old_ranges || true)"`; lib/annotate.sh:284 `[[ -z "$ln" || -z "$ranges" ]] && return 1`
suggested_fix: Capture `gh pr diff` into a variable and check its exit status and non-emptiness. On failure, print one 'diff unavailable, no hook annotations attempted' line and return, rather than treating empty ranges as 'not touched'.
needs_runtime_repro: Run the hook path on a PR whose `gh pr diff` fails (e.g. a mocked gh that exits 1) and observe the listed reasons.

summary: Annotate does an unlocked read-modify-write with the temp file in $TMPDIR, while a detached background `sync` runs for tens of seconds. A concurrent writer's `mv` silently discards the other's update.
failure_scenario: `gh pr merge N` spawns a background `sync` (post-bash-dispatch.sh:329) that reads the ledger and makes per-entry gh calls. The agent's next `git commit`, or an explicit `annotate-commit --pick`, writes and `mv`s the ledger. Sync later `mv`s its own tmp, built from the pre-annotation inode, over it. The annotation is lost although the CLI printed 'Annotated 1 entry', so a confirmed canonical annotation never arms the closer. The reverse order loses sync's flips. `mktemp -t` also puts the file in $TMPDIR, so `mv` is a cross-filesystem copy (not atomic) and the ledger ends up with mode 0600.
evidence: lib/annotate.sh:150 `tmp="$(mktemp -t found-issues.XXXXXX)"`, :172-174 `mv "$tmp" "$file"`; the same pattern is at :529-542 and in lib/sync.sh:94. There is no flock or lockdir anywhere in bin/ or lib/ (searched for flock, lockdir and fi_lock).
suggested_fix: Create the tmp beside the ledger (`mktemp "$file.XXXXXX"`) and take a mkdir-based lock (portable to bash 3.2 and Git Bash) around read-through-mv in annotate, sync, resolve and defer. At minimum, re-check that the ledger is unchanged (cksum) before `mv`.
needs_runtime_repro: Run `found-issues sync` with a slow gh stub in the background, run `annotate-commit --pick` mid-sync, wait for sync to finish, and check whether the annotation survives.

summary: `git show --name-only` quotes non-ASCII or special paths (default core.quotePath) as `"dir/caf\303\251.md"`. Those never match the entry's real path, and the diff header paths have the same problem.
failure_scenario: Entry `- [open] ... docs/café.md:12 — typo`. A commit edits that file. touched_files contains the literal string `"docs/caf\303\251.md"` with quotes, so there is no match and the annotation is silently skipped. In `fi_diff_old_ranges`, a quoted `--- "a/caf\303..."` path also never matches.
evidence: lib/annotate-commands.sh:267 `git show --name-only --format= "$full_sha" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^$'` (no `-z` and no `-c core.quotepath=off`); :276 `git show --format= "$full_sha" | fi_diff_old_ranges`
suggested_fix: Use `git -c core.quotepath=off show ...` for both calls, and strip the `a/` prefix explicitly. Consider `--no-ext-diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` so user diff.noprefix and mnemonicPrefix configs cannot change the parsing.
needs_runtime_repro: Commit a change to `café.md`, log an entry on it, and run `annotate-commit HEAD`.

summary: The 'already annotated' test is a whole-line substring match, and the default non-hook path ignores an existing suggestion token. The result is either a silent skip or a duplicate canonical tag next to a stale PR-auto tag.
failure_scenario: (a) An entry whose symptom narrative quotes `(PR: org/repo#7)` or `(commit: abc1234)` counts as already annotated for that ref. `--pick`/auto report 'already annotated. No changes' and exit 0, but sync reads only the annotation tail, so the entry never closes. (b) For an entry carrying `(PR-auto: o/r#7)` from the hook, a plain `annotate-pr 7` or `--all` tests only the canonical form, so the entry is a candidate. It gets `(PR-auto: o/r#7) (PR: o/r#7)`, and sync keeps reporting the stale 'suggested ... has merged' line. `--pick` correctly replaces the token in place; the auto and `--all` paths do not.
suggested_fix: Test `fi_annotation_tail "$line"` instead of the full line. In the non-hook auto/`--all` path, promote an existing auto token in place, as `fi_annotate_apply_picks` does at lines 158-162.

summary: Ledger discovery walks up past the git repo root, so a repo or submodule with no ledger annotates an ancestor directory's ledger. `log`, `resolve` and `defer` are git-root-bounded, so they disagree with annotate.
failure_scenario: Repo B (nested checkout or submodule) has no docs/found-issues.md, but the enclosing directory or parent repo A does. Every `git commit` in B runs `annotate-commit HEAD --hook-auto`. It resolves A's ledger and matches B's touched files against A's entry paths by suffix (e.g. a bare `index.ts`). It writes `(commit-auto: <B sha>)` into A's ledger, and a manual `annotate-commit` writes a canonical `(commit: <B sha>)` that sync then cannot resolve in A.
evidence: lib/parse-entries.sh:27 `while [[ -n "$dir" && "$dir" != "/" ]]; do` (no git-toplevel bound); lib/annotate-commands.sh:123 and :249 `file="$(fi_find_issues_file)"`, versus bin/found-issues:228 `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel ...)"` in fi_resolve_issues_file
suggested_fix: In the annotate commands, stop the walk at `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, or reject a ledger that lies outside the current repo.
needs_runtime_repro: Put a docs/found-issues.md in a parent dir, `git init` a child with no ledger, commit a file that matches an entry suffix, and run the hook command.

summary: The confirm command the hook prints is `found-issues annotate-commit HEAD --pick ...`, with the literal word HEAD. Run after any later commit, it stamps the canonical, closing `(commit: <new HEAD>)` instead of the suggested commit.
failure_scenario: The agent commits A, and the hook prints 'Confirm the ones commit A fixes: found-issues annotate-commit HEAD --pick a.sh:5'. The agent commits B, then runs the printed command. HEAD is now B, so a.sh:5 gets `(commit: B)` canonical. The old `(commit-auto: A)` is not replaced because the auto form is derived from B, so both tokens remain. The entry is armed to close on whatever commit B is, not the one that fixed it. The same applies to the 'needs judgment' text and the `--all` hint.
suggested_fix: Build rerun_cmd with `$short_sha` (or the full sha) instead of `$target` when the target is a symbolic ref such as HEAD.
needs_runtime_repro: Run the hook on commit A. Make commit B. Run the printed command and inspect the ledger line.

summary: `fi_repo_id`'s sed prints the URL unchanged when it does not match, or captures the wrong segment. Malformed or wrong `(PR: ...)` refs can be written, and annotate-pr still reports success.
failure_scenario: For `ssh://git@github.com:22/org/repo.git`, `github\.com[:/]` matches `github.com:` and the capture becomes `22/org`. The annotation `(PR: 22/org#7)` is well-formed, so sync queries the wrong repo. For `git@github.com-work:org/repo.git` (ssh host alias), sed does not match and prints the whole URL, so repo_id is `git@github.com-work:org/repo`. The PR-existence check may pass if GH_REPO is set, and the annotation written is one the `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/...` regexes never recognise. GitHub Enterprise hosts (`github.mycorp.com`) fail the `*github.com*` test outright.
suggested_fix: Validate the sed result against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and return 1 otherwise. Optionally obtain the repo from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`, which already resolves aliases, ports and forks.
needs_runtime_repro: Set `git remote set-url origin ssh://git@github.com:22/org/repo.git` and run `found-issues annotate-pr 7 --pick x:1` with gh stubbed. Observe the annotation text.

summary: The commit route treats a missing `.tool_response.exit_code` as success. A failed or no-op `git commit` then annotates the previous HEAD.
failure_scenario: If the harness payload lacks `exit_code` (the code assumes it may), `git commit` with nothing staged, or one rejected by a pre-commit hook, passes the gate. `annotate-commit HEAD --hook-auto` runs on the old HEAD. On the default branch the annotate-commit default-branch guard does not apply, so `(commit-auto: <old sha>)` suggestions get recorded and later reported by sync as 'suggested ... has landed'. The regex at :277 also matches `git commit` text inside echo or quoted strings.
suggested_fix: Compare HEAD before and after (record `git rev-parse HEAD` in a PreToolUse, or compare against the last-annotated sha in the state dir). Alternatively require stdout to match `^\[[^]]+ [0-9a-f]{7,}\]`.
needs_runtime_repro: Dump a real PostToolUse(Bash) payload on Claude Code and Codex to see whether exit_code exists. Run `git commit` with nothing staged on the default branch and check whether a suggestion appears.

summary: `annotate-commit` resolves the default branch (including a network `gh repo view` fallback) on every invocation, including every `--hook-auto` post-commit run. Failures are never cached.
failure_scenario: In a repo created with `git init` plus `git remote add`, origin/HEAD is unset. Each `git commit` runs `fi_resolve_default_branch`, which runs `fi_repo_id`, `gh repo view` and `jq`. The cache only stores successes. Offline or unauthenticated, every commit pays a gh network timeout before the annotate pass. Even when online, the cache expires hourly and costs one gh call, though the guard only matters for manual annotate-commit on a feature branch.
evidence: lib/annotate-commands.sh:234-239 `if [[ "$force" != "yes" ]]; then ... default_branch="$(fi_resolve_default_branch)"`; bin/found-issues:312-318 (a result is cached only when non-empty)
suggested_fix: Skip the guard when `hook_auto=yes`. A just-created commit cannot already be on the default branch from a feature branch. Alternatively, use only the local `symbolic-ref` or `main`/`master` heuristics there, with no gh call.
needs_runtime_repro: `git init`, add a remote, disable the network, and time `found-issues annotate-commit HEAD --hook-auto`.

summary: On a CRLF ledger (Git Bash with autocrlf), annotations are inserted after the trailing CR. The entry ends up with a CR in the middle of the line and mixed line endings.
failure_scenario: `read -r` keeps the `\r` at the end of the entry, so `printf '%s %s\n' "$line" "$annotation"` writes `...(suggested: x)\r (PR: o/r#7)\n`. The tail regex tolerates this, but the `\r` is now mid-line. Exact-text matching (grep -Fx against auto_set, `[[ $line == $target ]]` in other mutators) is fragile on such lines. Later stages produce diffs and an LF-only line next to CRLF ones.
suggested_fix: Strip a trailing `\r` before appending (`line=${line%$'\r'}`) and re-add it afterwards if the original line had one.
needs_runtime_repro: Convert docs/found-issues.md to CRLF, run `annotate-commit --pick path:line`, and inspect the result with `od -c`.
